questions.stem: Which of the following is a secondary activity?
questions.explanation: Secondary activities change raw materials into finished products or structures, and construction belongs to this group along with manufacturing. Fishing and collecting honey take material directly from nature (primary), while running a railway is a service (tertiary).

optionRationale.1: Fishing takes a product directly from water, so it is primary.
optionRationale.3: Running a railway provides a transport service, so it is tertiary.
optionRationale.4: Collecting honey is a gathering activity and so primary.

questions.stem: A large estate growing a single cash crop such as tea or rubber, mostly for export, is an example of
questions.explanation: Plantation agriculture is a form of commercial farming on large estates that specialise in one crop, usually for sale in distant markets, often with processing on or near the estate. Subsistence farming and herding aim mainly at the needs of the family or group.

optionRationale.1: Primitive subsistence farming, such as shifting cultivation, feeds the farmer's own family.
optionRationale.2: Nomadic herding is the movement of animals in search of pasture and water.
optionRationale.3: Intensive subsistence farming uses small holdings and much labour to feed the family.

questions.stem: Match the activity in List-I with the correct type in List-II.

left: A. A sugar mill crushing cane
B. Pottery made in a family courtyard
C. A tea estate with its own factory
D. Bakarwals moving flocks to high pastures in summer

questions.explanation: A sugar mill uses an agricultural raw material, so it is agro-processing. Pottery by a family at home is a household industry. A tea estate is plantation agriculture, and the seasonal movement of flocks between highland and lowland pastures is transhumance. Hence A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II.

optionRationale.2: This code treats the sugar mill as a household industry and the estate as transhumance.
optionRationale.3: This code reverses the sugar mill and the estate, and the pottery and the flocks.
optionRationale.4: This code gives transhumance to the sugar mill and plantation farming to the pottery.

questions.stem: Which description fits commercial grain farming?
options: Small plots tilled by hand in a crowded monsoon region, with most of the grain kept for the family's own food
Seasonal movement of flocks between hill pastures and the plains each year
Very large mechanised farms in thinly populated temperate grasslands, grown for sale
Clearing and burning a forest patch to grow food for a few years, then moving on to a fresh patch of forest
questions.explanation: Commercial grain farming is a modern agriculture type with very large farms, heavy use of machines and a surplus sold in the market. It is typical of thinly populated temperate grasslands. The other three descriptions are intensive subsistence farming, transhumance and shifting cultivation.

optionRationale.1: Small hand-tilled plots feeding the family describe intensive subsistence agriculture.
optionRationale.2: Seasonal movement of flocks is transhumance, a pastoral activity.
optionRationale.4: Clearing and burning forest is shifting cultivation.

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): In developed countries only a small share of the workforce is engaged in agriculture.
Reason (R): Farming in these countries is done by hand with simple tools, which needs a very large number of workers.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: In developed countries mechanisation, fertilisers and improved seeds allow a few farmers to cultivate large areas, so the farm workforce share is small. The assertion is therefore true. The reason is false, because such farming is highly mechanised and not done by hand with simple tools.

optionRationale.1: R is false, so it cannot explain A.
optionRationale.2: R is not true, so the option claiming both are true is wrong.
optionRationale.4: A is true, so the option calling it false is wrong.

questions.objective: Explain low farm employment in developed countries

questions.stem: A person collecting honey, nuts and roots from a tropical forest is engaged in
questions.explanation: Gathering means collecting products such as nuts, fruits, roots and honey that nature provides, usually with simple tools. Because the material is taken directly from nature, gathering is a primary activity. It is not farming, manufacturing or a knowledge-based activity.

optionRationale.2: Plantation agriculture involves planting and managing a crop on an estate.
optionRationale.3: Household manufacturing changes raw material into goods at home.
optionRationale.4: Knowledge-based work belongs to the quaternary sector.

questions.objective: Identify gathering as a primary activity

questions.stem:
Consider the statements.
A. Intensive subsistence agriculture is carried out on small holdings with much labour.
B. Plantation agriculture is usually aimed at distant markets.
C. A primitive subsistence farmer sells most of the produce in distant markets.
D. Large-scale industries use mass production with specialised labour.
Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements A, B and D are correct descriptions: intensive subsistence farming uses small holdings and much labour, plantations produce for distant markets, and large-scale industry relies on mass production and specialised labour. Statement C is false because a primitive subsistence farmer mainly consumes the produce.

optionRationale.1: C is false, so any option containing C is wrong, and this option leaves out B and D.
optionRationale.2: C is false and this option also omits A and D.
optionRationale.3: C is false, so all four cannot be correct.

questions.objective: Evaluate statements on farming and industry types

questions.stem: Dairy farming is commonly developed near large urban markets mainly because
options: cattle can graze only in towns
milk and milk products are perishable and must reach buyers quickly
dairy cattle need very hot and dry conditions to produce milk
milk is mainly exported to other continents by ship
questions.explanation: Milk and its products spoil quickly, so dairy farms are located close to towns or have fast transport and cold storage. Urban demand also provides a ready market. Cattle do not need towns for grazing, and milk is not mainly shipped across continents.

optionRationale.1: Cattle graze on pastures and fodder crops, not specifically in towns.
optionRationale.3: Dairy cattle do best in cool, moist conditions with good fodder, not hot and dry ones.
optionRationale.4: Fresh milk is mostly sold in nearby markets, not shipped across oceans.

questions.objective: Explain the location of dairy farming

questions.stem: Which statement about large-scale manufacturing industry is correct?
options: It uses large capital, assembly-line mass production and specialised labour
It depends only on family labour working with simple tools in the home of the worker
It makes goods only for the local village market using local material
It needs no transport because production is done close to the buyers
questions.explanation: Large-scale industries such as iron and steel, textile mills and car assembly need large capital, specialised labour and heavy machinery, and they mass produce goods for wide markets. Family-based work with simple tools describes household industry, and village-market production describes cottage or small-scale units.

optionRationale.2: Family labour with simple tools describes a household industry.
optionRationale.3: Production only for a local market with local material describes small cottage units.
optionRationale.4: Large industries depend heavily on transport for raw material and markets.

questions.stem: In year A a region has 40 million workers, 30 per cent of them in tertiary activities. In year B it has 50 million workers, 40 per cent in tertiary activities. By what percentage did the number of tertiary workers increase?
questions.explanation: Tertiary workers in year A = 0.30 x 40 = 12 million. In year B = 0.40 x 50 = 20 million. The increase is 8 million, and 8/12 x 100 is about 67 per cent. The rise in the share is only 10 percentage points, which is a different measure.

optionRationale.1: 10 is the rise in the percentage share, not the rise in the number of workers.
optionRationale.2: 8 million is not one third of 12 million.
optionRationale.4: A 100 per cent rise would need 24 million tertiary workers in year B.

questions.objective: Compute percentage change in sector employment

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Tertiary activities gain importance as an economy develops.
Reason (R): Primary activities are the oldest economic activities practised by human beings.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: As incomes rise, people demand more trade, transport, education and health services, so the tertiary share grows. It is also true that primary activities are the oldest. But their age does not explain why services expand, so R is true but not the explanation of A.

optionRationale.1: Age of primary activities does not explain the growth of services.
optionRationale.3: R is a true statement, so calling it false is wrong.
optionRationale.4: A is true, so the option calling it false is wrong.

questions.objective: Relate economic development to the growth of services

questions.stem: Which sequence best describes the usual change in the shares of workers as an economy develops from an agrarian base to an advanced one?
options: Primary rises, secondary falls, tertiary stays the same
Primary and secondary both rise steadily, tertiary falls
Primary rises first and then falls, while quaternary stays the lowest and remains constant throughout
Primary falls steadily, secondary rises and later declines, tertiary and quaternary rise
questions.explanation: In the usual pattern, mechanisation and rising incomes reduce the share of primary workers. Secondary employment grows during industrialisation and later declines as services expand, while tertiary and quaternary shares keep rising in advanced economies. The other sequences contradict this pattern.

optionRationale.1: Primary employment does not rise as a country develops.
optionRationale.2: Tertiary share rises, it does not fall, with development.
optionRationale.3: Primary falls with development and quaternary grows in advanced economies.

questions.objective: Trace the shift of employment across sectors

questions.stem: A region has very low population density, vast natural grassland and cheap land, and its meat is sent to distant markets in refrigerated vehicles. The most likely activity is
questions.explanation: Commercial livestock ranching needs large areas of cheap grassland with few people, and it produces meat and wool for distant markets with modern transport and storage. Subsistence rice farming needs dense population, while market gardening is intensive farming of vegetables near towns.

optionRationale.1: Intensive rice farming needs dense population and small holdings.
optionRationale.2: Shifting cultivation is for subsistence and is not market oriented.
optionRationale.3: Market gardening is intensive and sited near cities, not on vast grassland.

questions.objective: Infer an activity from geographical conditions

questions.stem: Match the work in List-I with its sector in List-II.

left: D. Data analysis and research and development

questions.explanation: Fishing takes a product from water, so it is primary. Cement manufacture changes raw material into a product, so it is secondary. Tourism supplies a service, so it is tertiary, and data analysis with research and development is knowledge work, so it is quaternary.

optionRationale.1: This code treats cement manufacture as tertiary and tourism as secondary.
optionRationale.3: This code treats fishing as secondary and cement manufacture as primary.
optionRationale.4: This code treats tourism as quaternary and research as tertiary.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a feature of modern (commercial) agriculture?
options: Crops grown mainly for the farmer's own food
Use of animal manure only, with no market sale
Use of machinery and high-yielding seeds, with crops grown mainly for sale
Burning forest and abandoning the plot after a few years
questions.explanation: Modern or commercial agriculture grows crops mainly for sale and uses machinery, high-yielding seeds, fertilisers and the market. Growing food for the family and shifting cultivation belong to subsistence agriculture.

optionRationale.1: Growing for the farmer's own food is subsistence farming.
optionRationale.2: Commercial farming sells its produce and uses modern inputs.
optionRationale.4: Burning forest and abandoning plots is shifting cultivation.

questions.stem:
Consider the statements on quaternary activities.
A. They deal with knowledge, information and research.
B. They need large numbers of unskilled workers.
C. Knowledge-based industries depend mainly on skilled people.
Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Quaternary activities concern knowledge, information and research, and knowledge-based industries such as software depend on educated, skilled people. So A and C are correct. Statement B is wrong because these activities need skilled workers and not large numbers of unskilled ones.

optionRationale.2: B is false, so any option containing it is wrong.
optionRationale.3: B is false and A is true, so this pair is wrong.
optionRationale.4: B is false, so all three cannot be correct.

questions.stem: In a district of 500 workers, 30 per cent are in primary and 45 per cent in secondary activities; the rest are in tertiary activities. The ratio of secondary to tertiary workers is
questions.explanation: Secondary workers are 45 per cent of 500, which is 225. Tertiary share is 100 - 30 - 45 = 25 per cent, which is 125 workers. The ratio 225 : 125 simplifies to 9 : 5 on dividing both by 25.

optionRationale.3: 5 : 9 is the inverse ratio, tertiary to secondary.
optionRationale.4: 2 : 1 would need 250 secondary workers against 125 tertiary workers.

questions.objective: Compute a ratio from sector percentages

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a primary activity?
options: Fishing in coastal waters and rivers
Forestry, including felling and collecting wood
Weaving cloth in a textile mill
Pastoralism, rearing animals on natural pastures
questions.explanation: Primary activities extract or produce materials directly from nature, as in fishing, forestry and pastoralism. Weaving cloth in a mill turns yarn into a finished product, which is manufacturing and so a secondary activity.

optionRationale.1: Fishing takes a product directly from water and is primary.
optionRationale.2: Forestry works directly with forest resources and is primary.
optionRationale.4: Pastoralism is the rearing of animals and is primary.
